stepDescriptions: Verify Linux 7.0.0 or newer, UEFI Secure Boot, encrypted storage, hibernation capacity, and the official fallback kernel.
Review the update policy, retained project kernels, and optional TPM configuration before making changes.
Check the latest project Release, download the kernel and headers, then verify its signed manifest, package signatures, and permitted version.
Prepare the project certificate for firmware enrollment.
Install the kernel packages, headers, updater services, and exact-kernel resume boot path.
Restart into the project kernel and verify Secure Boot, lockdown, signatures, and the Ubuntu fallback path.
Enroll the final PCR 7 policy, test TPM-only unlock, and confirm that password recovery remains available.

details.mokOneTimePasswordDescription: Record this password before restarting. It is required once by MokManager.
details.updatePolicyDescription: Select behavior supported by the installed systemd controller.
details.kernelRetentionDescription: Choose how many previous project kernels remain after an update; official Ubuntu kernels are never removed.
details.fallbackLockedDescription: Always retained and continues to be managed by APT.
details.configureTpmDescription: Enroll only after the final project-kernel PCR 7 state has been verified.
details.configureTpmAria: Configure TPM automatic unlock after installation
details.crypttabDescription: This read-only check does not prove that a TPM token can unlock the volume.
details.runningKernelHelp: Why: this project requires Linux 7.0.0 or newer. How: install and boot a supported Ubuntu kernel before continuing.
details.secureBootHelp: Why: the project-signed kernel is verified through UEFI Secure Boot. How: enable Secure Boot in firmware settings, then check again.
details.lockdownHelp: Why: Kernel Lockdown prevents privileged software from bypassing the Secure Boot trust chain through low-level kernel access. How: enable Secure Boot, then boot an official Ubuntu kernel or a project-signed kernel that supports Lockdown and check again.
details.luksHelp: Why: hibernation writes session memory, application data, and potentially key material to Swap. Without LUKS, an offline party can read that image. How: use an encrypted Ubuntu installation or migrate the root volume manually. Installation may continue without it.
details.hibernationSpaceHelp: Why: suspend-to-disk needs a disk-backed Swap file at least as large as physical memory. How: select Fix Automatically to create or replace /swap.img safely.
details.officialFallbackHelp: Why: an official Ubuntu kernel provides an independent recovery boot path. How: install the Ubuntu HWE kernel meta-package before continuing.
details.tpmUnavailableWithoutLuks: TPM automatic unlock is not applicable without a LUKS root volume.
